title: Earthquakes for kids
examples: Teacher, why does the ground shake during an earthquake?
What should we do if the ground starts shaking?

explain.say: The Earth's surface is not one solid piece. It is broken into big puzzle pieces.
These big puzzle pieces are called tectonic plates. They float slowly on the Earth.
When these giant plates move past each other, they can get stuck and then slip. This causes shaking.
When the ground shakes, it is an earthquake. This shaking is what we feel on the ground.
If you feel shaking, the first thing to do is drop down to the floor. This keeps you safe.
If you are outside, move to an open area away from buildings. Stay safe from falling things.

faq.q: Why does the ground shake during an earthquake?
faq.a: The ground shakes because the giant puzzle pieces of the Earth move. These pieces are called tectonic plates, and when they move, they can cause shaking.

faq.q: What should we do if the ground starts shaking?
faq.a: You should immediately drop down to the floor. Then, cover your head and neck with your arms. After that, hold on until the shaking stops.
asks: What is the safety rule for shaking?
Should I run outside right away?
What do I do during an earthquake?

faq.a: Sometimes, they can happen in the same area. Earthquakes happen because of plate movement, and volcanoes can also be linked to plate boundaries.
asks: Do earthquakes mean there will be a volcano?
Are these two things always together?
What is the link between volcanoes and shaking?

faq.q: Is it okay to stand near a big tree during shaking?
faq.a: No, it is not safe to stand near big trees. You should move away from things that can fall down, like trees or walls.
asks: Where is the safest place to be?
Should I hide under a table or near a tree?
What should I avoid during shaking?

faq.q: Do all parts of the Earth move?
faq.a: No, the movement is mostly in the large plates on the surface. These plates are what we call the tectonic plates.
asks: What part of the Earth moves?
Are there parts that do not move?

facts: The Earth's surface is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates.
Earthquakes happen when these plates move or slip past each other.
The safety action is to drop down, cover your head, and hold on.
It is safer to be in an open area during an earthquake.

quiz.say: The giant puzzle pieces that make up the Earth's surface are called:
quiz.why: These large pieces are what float and move slowly on the Earth.

wrong.0: This is a general term, but 'tectonic plates' is the specific scientific name.
wrong.1: This is too simple; the scientific term is needed.
wrong.3: The mantle is deep inside the Earth, not the surface pieces.

quiz.say: If you feel the ground shaking inside a building, what is the best immediate action?

options.show: Wait for the shaking to stop
options.say: Wait for the shaking to stop

quiz.why: This action protects your body from falling objects when the shaking starts.

wrong.0: You must take action as soon as you feel the shaking start.
wrong.2: You might hit falling debris while running out.
wrong.3: Doorways are not strong enough to protect you from falling items.

quiz.say: If you are outside when the ground shakes, where should you move?

options.show: An open area away from buildings
options.say: An open area away from buildings

quiz.why: Open areas keep you away from falling objects like walls or trees.

wrong.0: These areas might trap you or not be safe from falling debris.
wrong.2: Large trees can fall over during strong shaking.
wrong.3: Walls can collapse or fall onto you.
